rationale: Tests ability to choose the appropriate risk score depending on clinical context — a core apply-level competency in GI bleeding triage
Tests understanding of the restrictive transfusion threshold — a high-yield fact that directly impacts patient safety in GI bleeding management
Tests application of structured history-taking in GI bleeding — specifically identifying which medication history detail most alters differential diagnosis
Tests understanding of postural hypotension as a volume assessment tool — a clinically important bedside sign in GI bleeding
Tests recall of Forrest classification used in endoscopic risk stratification — a named scoring system students must know exactly
Tests application of endoscopy timing principles — knowing when endoscopy is urgent vs. elective is a key clinical decision point
Tests application of transfusion decision-making — specifically the restrictive threshold and its modification in cardiovascular disease
Tests understanding of the variceal pharmacological bundle — specifically whether antibiotics are part of the evidence-based management package
